newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Taiwan futures ease despite ban news.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Taiwan futures ease despite ban news.

text.p: SIMEX Taiwan stock index futures ended easier in relatively slow trade on Wednesday but traders were cautiously optimistic about news Taiwan was moving towards legalising local trading of the offshore futures.
The MSCI Taiwan May contract ended at 349.2 against its opening 353.4 on volume of 1,277 lots. The contract traded at a discount of nine points to the cash index for much of the day.
Sentiment was bearish with many traders looking for a further pullback during the week, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily market commentary.
Dealers said the market showed little immediate reaction to news that Taiwan's Finance Ministry had approved a proposal to lift a ban on trading of offshore stock index futures.
A ministry official said the proposal would be submitted to the cabinet for approval as soon as possible.
SIMEX traders said the news was positive for the market but unlikely to have any real impact until the ban was actually lifted.
Futures traders in Taiwan said cabinet approval was expected by June 1.
The Taiwan stock market's daily trading volume has averaged well above T$100 billion in recent months, and dealers said investors would use the stock index futures to hedge risk.
Analysts have estimated Taiwan stock-index futures trading could pour T$50 billion a month into offshore markets in Singapore and Chicago.
Nikkei futures surged over 700 points to close at their highest level since January 6 on Wednesday following the Dow's hefty overnight gains.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract added 775 points to end 10 points shy of its intra-day high of 19,400. Market turnover was a healthy 22,000 lots.
Dealers said the market was propelled higher by buying by a Japanese investment trust and stop-loss purchases above the 19,250 level, which had been expected to pose a stiff barrier.
"We heard a Tokyo investment trust was buying so the market went higher especially after it broke 19,250," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the market showed potential to come off by the end of the week as players might not want to stay long ahead of a Japanese holiday on Monday.
But the June Nikkei was likely to be supported at 19,250 and then at 18,950, he said.
A trader with a local institution said the contract should hold above the 19,000 level and would need to break above immediate resistance at 19,550 to make further headway.
"The next strong objective is at 19,800 provided it takes out 19,550 first. For the moment, the market is showing more strength than expected," he said.
